entries.habitat: Frozen Pine Barrens & Ash Dunes
entries.observation: A lean, gray-pelted canid with a split cervical spine supporting two fully functional skulls. The left head generally maintains forward scent while the right scans the flank and sky. Pack vocalizations are polyphonic and disorienting across open snow plains. They do not run in blind rushes; instead, the pack maintains a staggered semi-circle fifty meters out, probing for lagging pack beasts or injured scavengers before committing to an assault.
entries.field_intel: High acoustic sensitivity (responds to 440 Hz lures). Spooked by bright magnesium flares thrown between the two heads, causing neurological coordination conflict. Harvest yields heavy insulating wolf pelts and lean meat requiring thorough desulfurization before consumption.
entries.trap_preference: Heavy spring-jaw snare baited with fresh offal.
entries.edibility: Edible if boiled in salt brine; liver is dangerously toxic due to accumulated heavy isotopes.

entries.habitat: Sub-surface clay strata and collapsed sewer culverts
entries.observation: Hairless, wrinkled rodents reaching forty centimeters in length, equipped with massive, chisel-like protruding incisors. Their eyes have completely atrophied beneath thick skin flaps. They navigate tunnel systems by clicking their incisors rapidly against stone ribs and reading seismic echoes through their sensitive footpads.
entries.field_intel: Vulnerable to subterranean pitfall traps and low-frequency vibration lures (120 Hz). Harmless unless cornered in tight tunnels where incisors can puncture leather gaiters. Meat is rich in sulfur and dense in calories (450 kcal per animal), suitable for bunker stews after prolonged soaking.
entries.trap_preference: Pitfall cage trap or wire deadfall placed at tunnel choke points.
entries.edibility: Edible stew meat; pelts are pliable for light gaskets and insulating mittens.

entries.habitat: Industrial foundry slag heaps and coal rail yards
entries.observation: Heavy coleopterans up to sixty centimeters across, sporting layered chitin impregnated with sintered iron oxides and silica slag. They burrow into smoldering ash mounds to feed on anaerobic fungal mats and mineral salts. When disturbed, they vent superheated sulfur dioxide gas from rear spiracles with a sharp hiss.
entries.field_intel: Immune to small-caliber ballistics on dorsal carapace; soft ventral plate is vulnerable when overturned. Chitin plates can be harvested for industrial armor shingling and thermal baffles. Inedible meat, but carcass yields valuable combustible insect tallow.
entries.trap_preference: Crude deadfall weighted with rail iron; baited with sulfurous coal slurry.
entries.edibility: Inedible / toxic chemical glands; harvest solely for chitin and tallow.

entries.habitat: Dead urban canopies and ruined telephone pole corridors
entries.observation: Soot-black corvids with keratinized epidermal scales along the beak and crown. Flocks congregate in roosts of twenty or more above contaminated carcass dumps. They possess extraordinary memory for sniper hides and tripwire patterns, frequently dropping dry pebbles onto pressure plates to trigger deadfalls and feast on abandoned bait.
entries.field_intel: Can be dispersed with high-frequency acoustic emitters. Feathers accumulate heavy radioactive fallout dust; handling live birds without gloves causes localized contact radiodermatitis. Gizzards occasionally yield shiny scavenged brass tokens or small copper wire scraps.
entries.trap_preference: Clap-net or adhesive birdlime staged under dead roosts.
entries.edibility: Contaminated carrion bird; discard breast meat, harvest only salvage from crop.

entries.habitat: Crag summits, rocky overhangs, and ruined elevated roadways
entries.observation: Solitary feline predator with mottled slate-and-ochre camouflage, tufted ears, and hyper-elongated hind limbs designed for vertical bounding across cliff scree. Hunts by ambush from overhead masonry or rocky ledges, dropping onto caravan beasts to sever cervical arteries before retreating into inaccessible fissures.
entries.field_intel: Extremely wary of light sources and perimeter tripwires. Target with elevated watch posts; will break off pursuit if hit with high-energy kinetic fire before closing distance. Yields prime waterproof furs and heavy sinew for bowstrings and harness stitching.
entries.trap_preference: High-tension spring snare pinned to vertical climbing notches.
entries.edibility: Edible lean predator meat; bones yield dense carving stock.

entries.habitat: Reactor cooling ponds, industrial runoff channels, and estuary sludge
entries.observation: Bulky teleost fish covered in oversized, reflective silver-blue scales that deflect ambient thermal gradients. Thrives in warm, alkaline cooling sumps where heavy isotope concentrations kill normal aquatic life. Feeds on bacterial slime and heavy particulate sediments on reservoir bottoms.
entries.field_intel: Caught using baited heavy wire trotlines or gill nets. Gills and liver contain severe bio-accumulated cesium; fillet flesh must be stripped of red muscle fat and soaked in vinegar wash before boiling. Scales are tough enough to serve as light shim stock.
entries.trap_preference: Weighted gill net or wire trotline baited with molded mash.
entries.edibility: Conditionally edible; strict fillet dressing and lipid removal required.

entries.habitat: Slate quarry adits, limestone fissures, and abandoned elevator shafts
entries.observation: Colonial microbat with a wingspan exceeding 1.4 meters and a flattened, pug-nosed skull capable of biting through heavy canvas and thick work gloves. Colonies hang in massive clusters inside quarry ventilation shafts, emerging at dusk in swirling funnels that blot out the low radioactive cloud cover.
entries.field_intel: Vulnerable to smoke canisters and sulfur flares ignited at shaft portals. Bites carry high risk of hemorrhagic spore fever and bacterial sepsis. Harvest provides thick membranous leather and concentrated guano nitrate for gunpowder manufacture.
entries.trap_preference: Mist net strung across shaft entrances during dusk emergence.
entries.edibility: Toxic blood profile; harvest exclusively for leather and saltpeter guano.

entries.habitat: Dead pine needles, rotted roof rafters, and dense brushwood
entries.observation: Arachnid parasite ranging from the size of a walnut to a fist when fully engorged. Possesses heat-sensing pits capable of detecting a warm-blooded body through thirty meters of dead forest undergrowth. Drops from branch perches directly onto neck napes and unsealed respirators.
entries.field_intel: Avoid areas with heavy pine brush during warm wind periods. Must be removed by applying hot blade steel or kerosene to the scutum; pulling tears the mouthparts and causes immediate deep-tissue tissue necrosis. Abdomens can be processed into anticoagulant salve.
entries.trap_preference: Pheromone-doped sticky roll strips hung in cabin perimeters.
entries.edibility: Inedible / vector parasite; useful only for medical extract harvesting.

entries.habitat: Scrub oak foothills, root hollows, and marsh margins
entries.observation: Massive suid with a thick dorsal crest of metallic, silica-hardened bristles and reinforced cranial bone shields. Highly aggressive when rooting for subterranean mycorrhizal truffles, charging intruders without warning at speeds exceeding thirty kilometers per hour.
entries.field_intel: Do not engage frontally with light handguns; cranial plate deflects pistol rounds. Aim for the soft shoulder crease behind the ear. Yields abundant red pork, lard tallow for lubricants, and heavy bristled rawhide suitable for combat boots.
entries.trap_preference: Deep pitfall trench with iron spikes or heavy steel jaw snare.
entries.edibility: Excellent calorie-dense pork (3200 kcal); tusk ivory carves cleanly.

entries.habitat: Brine marsh reed beds, stagnant drainage canals, and wet basements
entries.observation: Slender pit viper up to 1.8 meters in length with an iridescent green-and-yellow scale pattern and a glowing tail tip that pulses with faint green chemiluminescence in stagnant water to lure amphibians, rats, and careless foragers.
entries.field_intel: Venom causes rapid systemic hemolysis and respiratory paralysis within four hours if untreated. Wear heavy vulcanized boots when wading marshes. Venom sacs are highly prized by apothecaries for formulating nerve-block surgical analgesics.
entries.trap_preference: Funnel basket trap set in reed channels baited with live mice.
entries.edibility: Snake meat is lean and safe once head and venom glands are excised.

entries.habitat: Taiga peat bogs, river valleys, and sub-alpine willow flats
entries.observation: Enormous herbivore standing 2.4 meters at the shoulder, boasting a double set of palmate antlers and protruding lower canine tusks used for tearing bark and defending against wolf packs. Normally solitary, bulls become violently territorial during the autumn rut.
entries.field_intel: Capable of crushing light expedition vehicles and overturning supply sleds. Maintain at least eighty meters distance. A single mature bull provides over five hundred kilograms of dressed venison, heavy tallow casks, and thick insulating hides.
entries.trap_preference: Deadfall log drop or coordinated rifle team ambush.
entries.edibility: Prime survival meat; heart and bone marrow provide essential vitamins.

entries.habitat: Mine galleries, collapsed rail tunnels, and subterranean crypts
entries.observation: Broad-shouldered, slope-backed pack hunter with pale gray hair and bone-crushing jaw mechanics capable of shearing structural timber and iron bolts. Emits a low, resonant guttural chuckle that reverberates through concrete pipes before a subterranean ambush.
entries.field_intel: Extremely sensitive to loud concussive blasts; flashbangs or industrial blasting caps will scatter packs through vent shafts. Bones from previous kills are splintered into sharp projectile shards. Pelts are coarse but effective for bunker rugs.
entries.trap_preference: Reinforced spring jaw trap bolted to tunnel floor ties.
entries.edibility: Tough, gamey meat requiring multiple spiced boils to be palatable.

entries.habitat: Ruined cathedral belfries, radio towers, and dead ash forests
entries.observation: Large nocturnal raptor with pure white plumage dusted with gray fallout ash, oversized forward-facing amber eyes, and completely silent wing beats. Perches on telecommunication towers to scan wasteland roads for small rodents and lone travelers.
entries.field_intel: Neutral unless its nesting perch is approached within ten meters. Screech disrupts radio telemetry audio channels for several seconds. Pellets regurgitated beneath roosts contain high concentrations of scavenged metal rings, small batteries, and bone fragments.
entries.trap_preference: Pole-mounted noose carpet on high masonry perches.
entries.edibility: Lean avian meat; feathers provide excellent insulation for cold-weather sleeping rolls.

entries.habitat: Flooded basement vaults, drainage pipes, and toxic sump sumps
entries.observation: Segmented, jawless aquatic parasite reaching two meters in length, equipped with concentric rings of keratin teeth and a powerful muscular suction disc. Lies in wait in sediment muck, latching onto legs of wading survivors to drain blood and pump necrotic digestive enzymes.
entries.field_intel: Avoid wading flooded corridors without thigh-high vulcanized rubber boots. If attached, slice the suction ring along the lateral margin with a hot blade. Muscle meat can be smoked over hardwood fires to render an edible, oily survival ration.
entries.trap_preference: Submerged wire fyke net baited with bloody offal.
entries.edibility: Smoked flesh is edible and calorie-dense; discard liver and digestive tract.

entries.habitat: Dry slag dunes, concrete rubble fields, and sunlit south-facing masonry
entries.observation: Compact, heavy-bodied serpent with horned supraocular scales and a pale, ash-grey disruptive camouflage that renders it virtually invisible against powdered fallout dust. Coils beneath warm flat stones, striking when stepped on with lightning speed.
entries.field_intel: Check all sun-warmed rubble slabs before sitting or scavenging. Carry carbolic wash to neutralize localized venom necrosis. Snake skin provides fine water-resistant leather for holster wraps and precision tool pouches.
entries.trap_preference: Sunken tin-can pitfall traps along rubble perimeter paths.
entries.edibility: Clean, tender white meat; safe to roast over charcoal after removing head.

entries.habitat: Fast-flowing mountain streams, tailraces, and weir ponds
entries.observation: Playful, semi-aquatic mustelid with reinforced dermal scutes along its spine that protect against predatory fish and eagle strikes. Lives in family holts hollowed beneath washed-out bridge footings, catching crayfish, carp, and fresh mussels.
entries.field_intel: Skilled indicator of clean, non-acidic stream flow. If otters are active in a creek, the water is generally filterable and free of heavy chemical poisons. Pelts provide the finest waterproof fur lining available in the region.
entries.trap_preference: Submerged wire box trap set at weir slide channels.
entries.edibility: Edible dark meat; pelt is exceptionally valuable in trade at salt and fur outposts.

entries.habitat: Outskirt settlements, refuse dumps, and burned rail depots
entries.observation: Descendants of domestic working dogs that have developed patchy hairlessness, thickened skin calluses, and pack hierarchies centered around ruined food silos. Wary of fire, but bold when hunting in packs of six or more against solitary travelers at night.
entries.field_intel: Can be deterred by throwing dried food scraps or firing warning shots into soft ground. Pack leaders can be tamed or pacified with consistent salt-cured meat offerings over several visits. Provide tough rawhide and bones for shelter glue production.
entries.trap_preference: Drop-door box trap baited with warm broth and marrow bone.
entries.edibility: Lean, tough meat; fat renders into effective boot waterproofing grease.

entries.habitat: Estuary mudflats, shallow lagoons, and cooling weir shallows
entries.observation: Tall, graceful wading bird standing nearly two meters tall on elongated, featherless black legs that resist chemical acid burns from industrial mud. Possesses a dagger-like bill capable of spearing large fish and swimming rodents with unerring accuracy.
entries.field_intel: Very skittish; takes flight with a harsh croak when approached within forty meters, alerting all nearby predators and patrols. Feathers can be processed into fine quills for codex bookkeeping and air filter pre-screens.
entries.trap_preference: Long-range precision rifle take or concealed water snare.
entries.edibility: Strong fishy taste; edible if roasted over aromatic birch charcoal.

entries.habitat: Deep limestone caverns, subterranean bunkers, and mountain adits
entries.observation: Colossal apex predator exceeding eight hundred kilograms, completely blind with heavily scarred facial plates and massive curved claws adapted for tearing reinforced security doors and stone vault bulkheads. Relies on acute olfactory reception and subterranean infrasound sensing.
entries.field_intel: Avoid direct engagement unless equipped with heavy armor-piercing calibers or high explosives. Set off decoy sirens at opposite ends of cave galleries to draw it away from target salvage chambers. Yields hundreds of kilograms of tallow, heavy fur pelts, and massive bone trophies.
entries.trap_preference: Multiple tethered heavy rail deadfalls with electric detonation.
entries.edibility: Heavy red meat; provides enough lard and calories to sustain a bunker for months.

entries.habitat: Subterranean fungal farms, abandoned textile mills, and damp basements
entries.observation: Gentle, oversized saturniid moth with a thirty-centimeter wingspan coated in glowing bioluminescent green dust. Swarms gather around low-voltage bunker wiring and LED indicator lights, fluttering silently in hypnotic circular spirals.
entries.field_intel: Completely harmless. Swarm dust glows for hours after contact and can be collected in glass vials to serve as spark-free night lanterns in methane-rich mine shafts. Cocoons yield durable, radiation-shielding raw silk thread.
entries.trap_preference: Low-wattage amber light trap suspended over funnel jars.
entries.edibility: Pupae are edible and high in protein; raw silk spins into tough suture thread.

entries.habitat: Hydroponic bay trays, fallow surface fields, and ash-enriched soil
entries.observation: Hardy cereal grain with pale translucent green stalks that exhibit faint green phosphorescence in dim light. The seed heads are twice normal size, producing dense, oil-rich flour with eighteen percent protein content. Highly tolerant of cold, drought, and radioactive topsoil.
entries.field_intel: Grain concentrates radioactive cesium in its outer husk. Requires triple parboiling with discarded rinse water or specialized milling before baking bread. Can be cultivated in bunker greenhouse trays with minimal nutrient slurry.
entries.trap_preference: Harvest with hand sickle at dusk when glow indicates seed maturity.
entries.edibility: Edible after triple parboiling or milling; provides durable flour.

entries.habitat: Wastewater drains, warm industrial sluices, and graywater sumps
entries.observation: Gelatinous black fronds growing across warm drainage troughs. Covered in microscopic sticky trichomes that snare sewer insects and small rodents, secreting a potent acidic digestive enzyme that dissolves organic tissue within six hours.
entries.field_intel: Inedible for humans. Cultivated inside wastewater filtration channels to eliminate pest insect infestations and digest floating organic solids. Dried kelp ash produces high-purity potash for soap and fertilizer synthesis.
entries.trap_preference: Rake from sump walls using iron hooks and heavy rubber gloves.
entries.edibility: Toxic / acidic; useful for pest control and chemical potash production.

entries.habitat: Vermiculite beds, industrial spoil heaps, and clay trenches
entries.observation: Fist-sized subterranean tubers with tough, waxy purple skins. The plant bio-accumulates dissolved lead and heavy metals entirely in the outer two millimeters of cork skin, leaving the dense white starch core clean and nutritious.
entries.field_intel: Must be peeled thickly with a sharp knife before boiling; eating unpeeled tubers leads to acute heavy metal poisoning within days. High yield in contaminated soil makes it a premier staple food crop for bunker communities.
entries.trap_preference: Spade harvest forty days after foliage yellowing.
entries.edibility: Completely safe when peeled; dense carbohydrate starch (1400 kcal/kg).

entries.habitat: Cardboard pulp troughs, rotted timber struts, and sewer ceilings
entries.observation: Broad, chalk-white bracket fungus that grows in layered tiers on rotting cellulose waste and damp mine timbers. Produces a pleasant almond aroma and releases zero toxic spores into enclosed ventilation systems.
entries.field_intel: One of the safest wild foraged food sources in the wasteland. Naturally rejects heavy radionuclides, containing negligible radiation uptake (under 35 Bq/kg). Can be eaten raw or sauteed in tallow without complex detox preparation.
entries.trap_preference: Slice base flush from wood grain with clean knife.
entries.edibility: Fully edible raw or cooked; excellent protein and vitamin B source.

entries.habitat: Concrete ventilation louvres, intake grates, and exhaust ducts
entries.observation: Crustose orange-yellow lichen forming powdery circular colonies on concrete intake ductwork. When dried by airflow, it sheds fine particulate microscopic spores that irritate mammalian alveolar sacs, inducing chronic coughing fits.
entries.field_intel: Must be scraped from intake grates regularly and treated with fungicide wash to prevent bunker respiratory outbreaks. Dried scrape powder can be distilled into an effective aerosol irritant for defensive traps.
entries.trap_preference: Scrape with steel spatula into sealed tin while wearing respirator.
entries.edibility: Respiratory toxin; inedible. Used in crafting defensive irritant bombs.

entries.habitat: Low-light hydroponic bays, damp cellars, and fallout shelters
entries.observation: Compact cruciferous leafy green with ruffled ivory leaves that lack green chlorophyll, photosynthesizing via alternate red carotenoid pathways under ultraviolet wavelengths.
entries.field_intel: Thrives in subterranean bunker hydroponics with very low electrical wattage. Rich in essential vitamin C and sulfur compounds that protect against scurvy and radiation sickness. Mild, crisp cabbage flavor.
entries.trap_preference: Cut outer leaves every two weeks to stimulate core growth.
entries.edibility: Fully edible; prime antiscorbutic vegetable for bunker diets.

entries.habitat: Foundry rail ballast, slag heaps, and rusted scrap vehicle lots
entries.observation: Tough perennial herb with serrated dark leaves and a taproot that binds to iron filings in industrial ballast. Roots are so dense with absorbed magnetite that compass needles deflect when placed near a freshly dug cluster.
entries.field_intel: Roots are pulverized and steeped in boiling water to create an astringent, styptic tonic that stops internal bleeding and seals open lacerations in emergency triage. Carries mild metallic aftertaste.
entries.trap_preference: Dig with mattock along rusted rail ties.
entries.edibility: Medicinal decoction; stops hemorrhaging and accelerates clotting.

entries.habitat: Enclosed vault arboretums, sheltered courtyards, and deep greenhouses
entries.observation: Dwarf grafted fruit tree with dark gray bark and sweet-scented white blossoms that survive in controlled greenhouse atmospheres. Produces crisp, red-blushed apples with dense sugar stores and hardy storage life.
entries.field_intel: Requires clean, demineralized water and regular pollinator hand-brushing. Fresh fruit dramatically boosts survivor morale and prevents depressive fatigue episodes during long winter lockdown cycles.
entries.trap_preference: Prune lateral shoots and prune suckers in early spring.
entries.edibility: Pristine edible fresh fruit; supreme trade value at wasteland markets.

entries.habitat: Moist greenhouse planters, spent compost beds, and dark bunker corners
entries.observation: Plump, brown-capped cultivated mushroom grown on sterilized straw compost and spent grain mash. Fast-growing fruiting bodies emerge within three days of humidity cycling.
entries.field_intel: Reliable staple yield in all bunker types. Contains high protein and amino acid ratios, making it the primary constituent of bunker meat-extender patties and emergency soups.
entries.trap_preference: Twist and pluck at stem base when veil tears.
entries.edibility: Fully edible and nutritious; can be dried for long-term ration storage.

entries.habitat: Greenhouse vermiculite troughs and deep soil planters
entries.observation: Hardy orange-fleshed sweet tuber with climbing vines that can be trellised against bunker walls. Tolerates temperature fluctuations down to four degrees Celsius.
entries.field_intel: High caloric yield per square meter of planter space. Rich in beta-carotene and complex starches that sustain heavy physical labor shifts in the shelter.
entries.trap_preference: Excavate root bed gently to avoid slicing tuber skin.
entries.edibility: Excellent staple food; can be roasted, mashed, or distilled into fuel alcohol.

entries.habitat: Surface agricultural clearings, greenhouse long-beds, and ash flats
entries.observation: Perennial cereal crop with extensive root rhizomes that penetrate frozen subsoil and regrow year after year without reseeding. Bred in pre-war agricultural experimental stations for survival in nuclear winter.
entries.field_intel: Extremely resistant to frost heave and acidic rain. Provides consistent grain harvests twice per year and stabilizes eroding wasteland topsoil against wind scour.
entries.trap_preference: Scythe harvest leaving ten centimeters of stubble for overwintering.
entries.edibility: Excellent grain crop; ground into dark, dense sourdough bread flour.

entries.habitat: Disturbed rubble piles, bomb craters, and graveyard margins
entries.observation: Coarse, foul-smelling biennial herb with sticky glandular hairs, dull yellow flowers with purple veins, and a thick, fleshy taproot loaded with tropane alkaloids.
entries.field_intel: Ingestion of raw root causes severe hallucinations, delirium, and fatal cardiac arrhythmia. In controlled laboratory pharmaceutical synthesis, extracted scopolamine is essential for compounding surgical sedatives and antispasmodics.
entries.trap_preference: Dig root wearing protective nitrile gloves; avoid touching eyes after handling.
entries.edibility: Severe poison raw; valuable precursor for pharmaceutical sedation compounds.

entries.habitat: Ridge saddles, trail confluences, and culvert exits
entries.observation: Heavy hair-choked droppings deposited high on exposed boulders or fence posts, coupled with vertical claw scratches on roadside telegraph poles. Fresh scat still steaming in frost indicates an active hunt within four hundred meters.
entries.field_intel: Reading scat composition reveals recent prey species and herd hunger. Chalky white scat indicates bone starvation and extreme predator aggression.
entries.trap_preference: Avoid setting unmasked meat bait along scent markers; use masking cedar smoke.
entries.edibility: Non-edible ecological sign.

entries.habitat: Foothill pine copses and scrub ravines
entries.observation: Uniform clean horizontal stripping of willow and poplar bark between one and two meters off the ground, leaving yellow inner sapwood exposed. Shows herd feeding height and density.
entries.field_intel: Sharp incisor gouges indicate passing goat herds; fresh resin seepage indicates passage within twenty-four hours, marking ideal snare ambush points.
entries.trap_preference: Position leg-hold snares along natural defiles leading into stripped copses.
entries.edibility: Inner poplar cambium is edible emergency survival forage.

entries.habitat: All surface sectors and transit corridors
entries.observation: Sudden, complete cessation of crow chatter and gull cries across a three-hundred-meter radius, accompanied by birds perching motionless in high power pylons.
entries.field_intel: Avian silence reliably signals an apex stalker (lynx or wolf pack) moving downwind. Expedition teams should immediately ready defensive firearms.
entries.trap_preference: Halt expedition march and form defensive circle.
entries.edibility: Non-edible ecological cue.

entries.habitat: Open ash flats, highway intersections, and river bars
entries.observation: Slow, tight spiraling flight of crows and gulls descending over a localized ground point, occasionally dipping below tree lines.
entries.field_intel: Indicates a large carcass, failed caravan, or freshly killed grazer. Offers high salvage potential but carries extreme risk of ambush by rival predators.
entries.trap_preference: Approach downwind with dosimeter drawn; inspect carcass for isotopic glow before butchering.
entries.edibility: Carcass may yield meat if not decomposed or tainted.

entries.common_name: Moth Cocoon Silks & Damp Soil Drills
entries.habitat: Alluvial floodplains, rotting silage, and damp basements
entries.observation: Web-like sticky silk strands spun between dry reeds, dotted with calcified white pupae cases anchored in moist sandy loam.
entries.field_intel: Silken webbing indicates an impending warm-damp swarm emergence. Warns agricultural stations to seal greenhouse air intakes before leaf-stripping larvae hatch.
entries.trap_preference: Burn silk nests with sulfur candles before adult emergence.
entries.edibility: Pupae are high in protein and lipids if roasted in dry ash.

entries.habitat: River crossings, marsh channels, and culverts
entries.observation: Deep mud wallows churned with split hoofprints, frothy saliva froth on bank reeds, and heavy musky scent hanging in cold air.
entries.field_intel: Marks the bottleneck crossing of a sounder during autumn mast migration. Highly productive heavy game ambush zone if intercepted at dawn.
entries.trap_preference: Heavy iron pitfall or staked fall trap baited with fermented grain mash.
entries.edibility: Boar meat provides calorie-dense pork and rendered lard.
